docs.title: Sequencing Level 3
docs.text:
A Sequencing Level 3 entry documents further-processed sequencing data derived from a Sequencing Level 2 alignment, such as count matrices or probe-level summaries. This level captures matrix-type metadata (raw, normalized, scaled, or batch-corrected counts), unique probe and target counts, and the workflow, software, and parameters used to generate the processed output.

Level 3 entries represent the analysis-ready data products most commonly used for downstream statistical analysis, while still preserving a clear lineage back to the Level 2 alignment and Level 1 raw reads that produced them.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Sequencing Level 3 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Sequencing Level 3 entries ensures that processed count data is documented with enough workflow and provenance detail for others to understand exactly how it was derived, and to confidently reuse it in downstream analyses shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Sequencing Level 3 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Computational Genomics Analysts – Document the workflow, parameters, and matrix type used to generate processed count data.
  2. Bioinformatics Pipeline Developers – Record the software and workflow versions that produced the processed outputs, supporting reproducibility.
  3. Research Staff – Track which processed data products correspond to which raw and aligned files.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for processed sequencing outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Sequencing RNA Level 1
docs.text:
A Sequencing RNA Level 1 entry documents raw, unaligned RNA sequencing data, extending the general Sequencing Level 1 structure with RNA-specific library metadata. In addition to standard NGS library and platform fields, this level captures RNA-specific details such as end bias (3 prime, 5 prime, or full-length transcript coverage), reverse transcription primer type, RNA integrity number (RIN), and DV200, which describe the quality and construction of the RNA library before sequencing.

These RNA-specific quality metrics are critical for interpreting downstream expression results, since RNA degradation or library construction choices can significantly affect quantification accuracy.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Sequencing RNA Level 1 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Sequencing RNA Level 1 entries ensures that raw RNA sequencing outputs carry the library construction and RNA quality metadata needed to properly interpret and reproduce downstream expression analyses shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Sequencing RNA Level 1 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Sequencing Core Staff – Record RNA library preparation details and quality metrics (RIN, DV200) at the point of library construction.
  2. Computational Genomics Analysts – Ensure RNA-specific metadata is available before it is used in expression quantification pipelines.
  3. Research Staff and Lab Managers – Track which raw RNA sequencing files correspond to which biospecimens and studies.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for raw RNA sequencing outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Study
docs.text: A Study entry documents key information about research projects, including methodologies, participants, and ethical considerations. Properly maintaining study records ensures that data is compliant with research standards, traceable, and usable across various scientific fields. This section explains how to create and maintain a valid study entry using the required fields, templates, and example data provided.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Study Entries
docs.text: Contributing study entries ensures that critical research details such as methodology, investigators, and related datasets are documented and accessible. This fosters transparency, collaboration, and reproducibility in research. A well-maintained study entry also helps stakeholders understand the scope, purpose, and outcomes of research efforts, enabling better data integration and analysis across projects.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Study Entries?
docs.text:
1. Principal Investigators (PIs) – Provide clear documentation of your studies to enhance visibility and demonstrate research contributions for funding agencies and collaborators.

  2. Research Coordinators and Project Leads – Ensure proper record-keeping of studies under your supervision, supporting compliance, reporting, and resource allocation.

  3. Data Managers – Create study entries to link related datasets, publications, and tools, improving data provenance and facilitating cross-references within research ecosystems.

  4. Consortium Participants – Contribute study information to showcase collaborative research efforts and track joint achievements.

  5. Funding Agencies and Grant Monitors – Monitor study progress by ensuring that all funded research is accurately documented and accessible.

  6. Ethics and Compliance Officers – Maintain study entries to verify that all necessary de-identification methods, IRB protocols, and data use policies are in place.

docs.title: Data Use Ontology (DUO) Implementation
docs.text:
MC2 Center uses the Data Use Ontology (DUO) to record the consent permissions and use restrictions that apply to data and materials. DUO terms are defined once, in the shared vocabulary (modules/shared/annotationProperty.csv and modules/shared/duo.csv). Full definitions for every term are on the Shared Standard Terms page.

Which attribute records DUO codes depends on the template:

Template Attribute Controlled list and companion fields? Study, File View, and the file-level assay templates (Imaging, Sequencing, NanoString GeoMx, Visium) Data Use Codes Yes DataDSP DSP Data Use Codes Yes Dataset View Dataset Data Use Codes No DataCatalog dataCatalogDataUseModifiers No

All four are multi-select, string-list attributes. Most values are real DUO term CURIEs (e.g. DUO:0000006, DUO:0000021), plus a Pending Annotation placeholder for records that have not yet been reviewed for data use restrictions. The Dataset View and DataCatalog attributes have no controlled list, so they never add companion fields; each value must still look like a DUO code (DUO:0000042, DUOPlus3) or be Pending Annotation.

docs.title: DUOPlus terms: Sage Bionetworks extensions to DUO
docs.text:
DUO does not have terms for a few governance concepts this model needs to track (deidentification method, data tier, license, etc.), so Sage Bionetworks defined seven extension terms, DUOPlus1 through DUOPlus7, that this model uses alongside the real DUO terms:

DUOPlus Term Governance Concept Companion Field DUOPlus1 Source geography sourceGeography DUOPlus2 Study population populationType DUOPlus3 Data deidentification deidentificationType DUOPlus4 Data permission dataPermission DUOPlus5 Data tier dataTier DUOPlus6 License License DUOPlus7 Attribution attribution

docs.title: How conditionally required fields are surfaced
docs.text:
Most DUO terms (e.g. DUO:0000042/General Research Use, DUO:0000006/Health or Medical or Biomedical Research) are self-contained labels — selecting one doesn't require anything else. A subset of terms, however, indicate that additional detail must be provided alongside the code. For these terms, the model links the code to a companion field: a separate attribute where the contributor records that detail. In the templates whose DUO attribute uses the controlled list (see the table above), selecting the code makes its companion field conditionally required; all other companion fields remain optional.

This conditional relationship is declared directly in modules/shared/annotationProperty.csv: each of these DUO/DUOPlus terms also appears there as its own Attribute row, and that row's DependsOn column names the companion field it requires. When the model is compiled to JSON Schema, each of these rows becomes an if/then rule on the DUO attribute — e.g. DataUseCodes containing DUO:0000026 requires UserSpecificRestriction to be filled in. json_schemas/Study.json has 14 such rules, one for each term below except DUOPlus6: Study always includes License, so it needs no rule.

DUO Term Meaning Companion Field (conditionally required) DUO:0000007 Disease-specific research diseaseSpecificResearch (MONDO ID) DUO:0000012 Research-specific restrictions researchSpecificRestrictions DUO:0000020 Collaboration required collaborationRequired (PI contact email) DUO:0000022 Geographical restriction geographicalRestriction (country code) DUO:0000024 Publication moratorium publicationMoratorium (end date) DUO:0000025 Time limit on use timeLimitOnUse (number of months) DUO:0000026 User-specific restriction userSpecificRestriction DUO:0000028 Institution-specific restriction institutionSpecificRestriction (ROR ID) DUOPlus1–DUOPlus7 Sage Bionetworks DUOPlus governance extensions (see table above) sourceGeography, populationType, deidentificationType, dataPermission, dataTier, License, attribution

For example, a Study entry with Data Use Codes set to DUO:0000024, DUO:0000022 must also provide values for publicationMoratorium (the moratorium end date) and geographicalRestriction (the applicable country code(s)) — but can leave every other companion field blank, since none of the other DUO/DUOPlus terms were selected.

docs.title: Tool
docs.text: A Tool entry documents software applications, utilities, or platforms designed to perform specific operations in research or technical workflows. These tools can include anything from data analysis programs to machine learning frameworks and bioinformatics utilities. Accurate documentation ensures that tools are easily discoverable, traceable, and appropriately integrated into research processes.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Tool Entries
docs.text: Contributing tool entries supports collaboration, reproducibility, and innovation by helping researchers and teams discover and use essential software for data analysis, visualization, and processing. Accurate documentation ensures tools are accessible and impactful across projects.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Tool Entries?
docs.text:
1. Developers – Share tools to boost adoption and integration.
  2. Researchers – Document tools for replicability and collaboration.
  3. Data Scientists – Ensure tools critical to workflows are recorded.
  4. Project Managers – Maintain visibility of tools used across teams.
  5. IT and Support Specialists – Provide operational details and support resources.

docs.title: Visium Auxiliary Files
docs.text:
A Visium Auxiliary Files entry documents supporting data associated with 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics experiments, such as aligned tissue images, quality control reports, and other files that accompany the primary sequencing and expression outputs of a Visium run. Rather than representing a sequencing or expression level itself, this module links auxiliary artifacts, such as slide images, scale factor files, and QC reports, back to the Visium RNA Level 1 through 4 files, biospecimen, and study they belong to, along with the run, slide, and capture area they were generated from.

Auxiliary files are often what make a Visium dataset interpretable and reusable: tissue images and QC reports give downstream users the context needed to evaluate spot detection, alignment quality, and tissue morphology alongside the expression data.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Visium Auxiliary Files Entries
docs.text: Contributing Visium Auxiliary Files entries ensures that the images, scale factors, and quality control artifacts generated during a Visium run are discoverable and properly linked to the sequencing and expression data they support, giving downstream users full context for interpreting spatial results shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Visium Auxiliary Files Entries?
docs.text:
1. Spatial Biology Researchers – Document tissue images and slide/capture area context generated during a Visium experiment.
  2. Computational Genomics Analysts – Record QC reports and scale factor files produced alongside spatial expression processing.
  3. Sequencing Core Staff – Track which auxiliary files correspond to which Visium run and biospecimen.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for auxiliary spatial transcriptomics files shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Visium RNA Level 1
docs.text:
A Visium RNA Level 1 entry documents raw RNA sequencing data associated with a Visium spatial transcriptomics spot/slide experiment. In addition to standard NGS library and platform fields, this level captures Visium-specific slide and library metadata, including the Visium run ID, spatial read content (spatial barcode and UMI vs. cDNA), spatial library construction method, capture area, slide version and ID, image re-orientation, and permeabilization time, along with RNA quality metrics such as RIN and DV200.

Because Visium data links sequencing reads to a specific physical location on a slide, accurate capture of the slide, capture area, and read-structure metadata at this level is essential for correctly reconstructing the spatial context of the data in downstream processing.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Visium RNA Level 1 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Visium RNA Level 1 entries ensures that raw spatial sequencing reads are documented with the slide, capture area, and library metadata needed to correctly reconstruct spatial context in downstream alignment and analysis shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Visium RNA Level 1 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Spatial Biology Researchers – Record slide, capture area, and permeabilization details from the Visium experiment.
  2. Sequencing Core Staff – Capture library preparation and platform metadata for the spatial sequencing run.
  3. Computational Genomics Analysts – Ensure raw file and slide metadata is complete before spatial alignment pipelines are run.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for raw Visium sequencing outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Visium RNA Level 2
docs.text:
A Visium RNA Level 2 entry documents the alignment workflow outputs downstream of a Visium RNA Level 1 file. This level captures the SAM tags used for the unique molecular identifier (UMI) and spatial barcode fields, a link to the spatial barcode whitelist file, whether hard trimming was applied, and the genomic reference, genome annotation, and workflow version used to perform the alignment.

Level 2 entries make explicit how raw spatial reads were mapped and tagged with their spatial barcodes, preserving the technical details needed to reproduce or audit the alignment step before expression quantification.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Visium RNA Level 2 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Visium RNA Level 2 entries ensures that the alignment and barcode-tagging workflow applied to spatial sequencing reads is documented with enough detail for others to reproduce or evaluate the analysis shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Visium RNA Level 2 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Computational Genomics Analysts – Record alignment tags, genomic reference, and workflow versions used to process spatial reads.
  2. Bioinformatics Pipeline Developers – Document the spatial barcode whitelist and trimming parameters applied during alignment.
  3. Spatial Biology Researchers – Confirm that aligned outputs are correctly linked back to the raw Visium run they originated from.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for aligned Visium sequencing outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Visium RNA Level 3
docs.text:
A Visium RNA Level 3 entry documents processed spatial transcriptomics data built from a Visium RNA Level 2 alignment together with its associated auxiliary files. This level captures per-spot summary statistics such as spots under tissue, mean reads per spatial spot, median genes and UMI counts per spot, sequencing coverage, and the proportion of reads mapped overall and to the transcriptome, along with the workflow version and file type generated.

These per-spot quality and summary metrics are what allow downstream users to assess the technical performance of a Visium run (e.g., tissue coverage, sequencing depth per spot) before interpreting the underlying biology.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Visium RNA Level 3 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Visium RNA Level 3 entries ensures that per-spot quality and summary metrics from a Visium run are documented, giving downstream users the information needed to assess data quality before further spatial analysis shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Visium RNA Level 3 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Computational Genomics Analysts – Record per-spot summary statistics and workflow versions produced by processing pipelines.
  2. Spatial Biology Researchers – Confirm that spot-level quality metrics accurately reflect the tissue and capture area analyzed.
  3. Bioinformatics Pipeline Developers – Document the file types and workflows used to generate processed spatial outputs.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for processed Visium sequencing outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Visium RNA Level 4
docs.text:
A Visium RNA Level 4 entry documents further-processed data built from a Visium RNA Level 3 output, capturing the generic workflow type and workflow parameters used to derive higher-order analysis products (e.g., spatial clustering, differential expression, or other downstream spatial analyses) from the per-spot summary data.

As the most highly processed level in the Visium cluster, Level 4 entries emphasize workflow provenance, ensuring that the analysis choices behind a derived spatial result remain traceable back through Level 3, Level 2, and Level 1 to the original tissue and sequencing run.

docs.title: Why You Should Contribute Visium RNA Level 4 Entries
docs.text: Contributing Visium RNA Level 4 entries ensures that downstream spatial analysis outputs remain traceable to the workflow and parameters that produced them, supporting reproducibility for results shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Who Should Be Contributing Visium RNA Level 4 Entries?
docs.text:
1. Computational Genomics Analysts – Document the workflow type and parameters used to generate derived spatial analysis products.
  2. Spatial Biology Researchers – Confirm that derived results are correctly linked back to the Level 3 data they were built from.
  3. Bioinformatics Pipeline Developers – Track workflow versions to support reproducibility across pipeline updates.
  4. Data Managers – Maintain consistent, portal-ready metadata for derived Visium analysis outputs shared through the CCKP.

docs.title: Attribute: Biospecimen Type Category
docs.text: Valid Value            Description                                                                                                                                               Ontology                                                                                                  Ascites                A biospecimen of ascitic fluid.                                                                                                                           NCIT:C159203 Blood                  A small volume of blood removed for testing or storage.                                                                                                   NCIT:C17610 Bone Marrow            A biological sample containing components collected from bone marrow of an experimental subject.                                                          NCIT:C164009 Cells                  A biospecimen comprised of purified or partially-purified cells.                                                                                          NCIT:C192998 Body Fluid or SubstanceMaterial produced by living organisms; a necessary constituent of, or product of, an organismal process.                                                  NCIT:C13236 Cell Line              A permanently established cell culture that will proliferate indefinitely given appropriate fresh medium and space.                                       NCIT:C16403 Central Nervous System The part of the nervous system that consists of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges.                                                                     NCIT:C12438 Mouth Rinse            A sample consisting of biological material from the buccal cavity, collected by introducing a solution into the mouth, swishing, and collecting the rinse.NCIT:C198712 Saliva                 The watery fluid in the mouth produced by the salivary glands that moistens food to aid digestion and helps protect the mouth against infection.          NCIT:C13275 Skin                   An organ that constitutes the external surface of the body, consisting of the epidermis, dermis, and skin appendages.                                     NCIT:C12470 Sputum                 A respiratory biospecimen obtained via expectoration.                                                                                                     NCIT:C189124 Stool                  Portion of semisolid bodily waste discharged through the anus.                                                                                            UBERON:0001988 Tissue                 A piece of tissue removed from an organism for examination, analysis, or propagation.                                                                     NCIT:C19697 Urine                  A biospecimen obtained from urine.                                                                                                                        NCIT:C189126 RNA                    A biospecimen consisting of isolated or enriched ribonucleic acid (RNA).                                                                                  NCIT:C198568 DNA                    A biospecimen consisting of extracted deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).                                                                                        NCIT:C449 Xenograft              A biospecimen derived from the culturing of a derived cell line in a non-human organism.                                                                  NCIT:C156443 Not Reported           Not provided or available.                                                                                                                                NCIT:C43234 Unknown                Not known, observed, recorded, or reported as unknown by the data contributor.                                                                            NCIT:C17998

docs.title: Attribute: Biospecimen Type
docs.text: Valid Value                                                          Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         Ontology                                                                                                  Additional - New Primary                                             A biospecimen collected from a new primary malignancy that arose in a patient in addition to a previously diagnosed primary tumor.                                                                                  NCIT:C156441 Additional Metastatic                                                A biospecimen derived from an additional metastatic tumor site, collected separately from the first-sampled metastatic lesion.                                                                                      NCIT:C156440 Analyte                                                              A substance or chemical constituent extracted or purified from a biospecimen that serves as the target of an analytical procedure, such as a nucleic acid or protein preparation.                                   NCIT:C128639 Benign Neoplasms                                                     A neoplasm that lacks the morphologic features of malignancy, such as severe cytologic atypia or tumor cell necrosis, and remains confined to its site of origin without metastasizing.                             MONDO:0005165 Blood Buffy Coat                                                     The fraction of an anticoagulated blood sample that contains most of the white blood cells and platelets following density gradient centrifugation of whole blood.                                                  BTO:0006181 Blood Clot                                                           A semisolid gelatinous mass of coagulated blood consisting of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets entrapped in a fibrin network.                                                                      UBERON:0010210 Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow                                   A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject that has been diagnosed with a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy.                                                                                              NCIT:C164015 Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow; Post-treatment                   A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject with a hematologic malignancy after the subject has received treatment.                                                                                             NCIT:C164017 Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood                              A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject that has been diagnosed with a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy.                                                                                   NCIT:C164030 Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood; Post-treatment              A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject with a hematologic malignancy after the subject has received treatment.                                                                                  NCIT:C164031 Blood Derived Liquid Biopsy                                          A blood-based liquid biopsy specimen used to sample circulating tumor cells, cell-free nucleic acids, or other tumor-derived material without a solid tissue biopsy.                                                NCIT:C135727 Blood Derived Normal                                                 A peripheral blood specimen collected from a subject that is used as a source of germline (non-tumor) DNA or as a matched normal control for genomic comparisons.                                                   NCIT:C17610 Body Fluid                                                           A liquid substance derived from the body, such as blood, urine, cerebrospinal fluid, or pleural effusion, that is collected as a biospecimen.                                                                       EMAPA:37441 Bone Marrow Normal                                                   A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject that does not contain malignant cells and is used as a normal reference sample.                                                                                     NCIT:C164009 Buccal Cell Normal                                                   A sample of normal (non-tumor) cells collected by scraping or swabbing the inside of a subject's cheek, commonly used as a source of germline DNA.                                                             NCIT:C172264 Cell                                                                 The smallest unit of living structure capable of independent existence, composed of a membrane-enclosed mass of protoplasm containing a nucleus or nucleoid.                                                        NCIT:C12508 Cell Line Derived Xenograft Tissue                                   A biospecimen derived from tissue that developed after a laboratory cell line was implanted and grown in a non-human host organism.                                                                                 NCIT:C156443 Cell Lines                                                           A permanently established cell culture that will proliferate indefinitely given appropriate fresh medium and growth space.                                                                                          NCIT:C16403 Control Analyte                                                      A biospecimen or analyte that is used as a comparator or reference against an experimental sample.                                                                                                                  NCIT:C156442 DNA                                                                  A long, linear, double-stranded polymer of nucleotides attached to a deoxyribose backbone that carries an organism's genetic information; used here to denote a specimen consisting of extracted DNA.          NCIT:C449 EBV Immortalized Normal                                              A biospecimen consisting of normal lymphocytes that have been infected in vitro with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cultured to establish an indefinitely proliferating cell line.                                    NCIT:C163993 Expanded Next Generation Cancer Model                                A next generation cancer model that has been expanded using tissue culture or other propagation methods.                                                                                                            NCIT:C184757 FFPE Recurrent                                                       A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue sample derived from tissue isolated from a subject with recurrent disease.                                                                                               NCIT:C172267 FFPE Scrolls                                                         A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue sample that has been cut on a microtome into a thin section that rolls up on itself, forming a scroll.                                                                   NCIT:C172268 Fibroblasts from Bone Marrow Normal                                  Fibroblast cells isolated from a normal (non-malignant) bone marrow specimen.                                                                                                                                       NCIT:C12482 GenomePlex (Rubicon) Amplified DNA                                   A DNA specimen that has been amplified using the GenomePlex (Rubicon Genomics) whole genome amplification method.                                                                                                   NCIT:C198569 Granulocytes                                                         A type of leukocyte with a multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic granules, subdivided into eosinophils, basophils, and neutrophils based on the staining properties of their granules.                                 NCIT:C12530 Human Tumor Original Cells                                           A sample comprised of cells that were isolated from a human tumor and have not been cultured or expanded.                                                                                                           NCIT:C172293 In Situ Neoplasms                                                    Neoplasms confined to the site of origin without invasion beyond the basement membrane or into surrounding tissue, such as carcinoma in situ.                                                                       NCIT:C36118 Lymphoid Normal                                                      A specimen of normal (non-malignant) lymphoid tissue or cells used as a reference or control sample.                                                                                                                NCIT:C13049 Metastatic                                                           A term referring to the clinical or pathologic observation of a tumor extension from its original site of growth to another anatomic site.                                                                          NCIT:C14174 Mixed Adherent Suspension                                            A sample comprised of a mixture of cells or clumps of cells, which may have been isolated from normal or tumor tissue, that are maintained together in a suspension culture.                                        NCIT:C174118 Mononuclear Cells from Bone Marrow Normal                            A biological sample containing mononuclear cells isolated from a normal (non-malignant) bone marrow specimen.                                                                                                       NCIT:C164011 Neoplasms of Uncertain and Unknown Behavior                          Neoplasms that, on morphologic grounds, cannot be classified with certainty as benign or malignant.                                                                                                                 NCIT:C65157 Next Generation Cancer Model                                         An approach to cancer modeling that utilizes clinical data as well as the genomic and transcriptomic profiles of the parent tumor, metastases, if present, and case-matched normal tissues from individual patients.NCIT:C172295 Next Generation Cancer Model Expanded Under Non-conforming ConditionsA next generation cancer model that has been expanded using unconventional or non-standard culturing methods.                                                                                                       NCIT:C184781 Not Allowed To Collect                                               An indicator that specifies that a biospecimen collection event was not permitted.                                                                                                                                  NCIT:C141478 Pleural Effusion                                                     Increased amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity, usually caused by lung infections, congestive heart failure, pleural or lung tumors, connective tissue disorders, or trauma.                                  NCIT:C3331 Post neo-adjuvant therapy                                            A biospecimen collected from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic agent.                                                                                                                        NCIT:C156444 Primary Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow                           A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject at the time of initial diagnosis of a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy, prior to treatment.                                                                   NCIT:C164015 Primary Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood                      A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject at the time of initial diagnosis of a hematologic malignancy, prior to treatment.                                                                        NCIT:C164030 Primary Tumor                                                        A tumor specimen collected from the anatomic site where the cancer originated, as opposed to a metastatic or recurrent site.                                                                                        NCIT:C8509 Primary Xenograft Tissue                                             Tissue derived from a patient's tumor that has been directly implanted and grown in a non-human host organism without prior in vitro culturing.                                                                NCIT:C122936 Recurrent Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow                         A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject at the time of relapse or recurrence of a hematologic malignancy.                                                                                                   NCIT:C164017 Recurrent Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood                    A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject at the time of relapse or recurrence of a hematologic malignancy.                                                                                        NCIT:C164031 Recurrent Tumor                                                      A tumor specimen collected after the reemergence of cancer at the original or a related site following a period of remission.                                                                                       NCIT:C4798 Repli-G (Qiagen) DNA                                                 A genomic DNA specimen that has been amplified from a limited-quantity sample using the REPLI-g (Qiagen) whole genome amplification technology.                                                                     NCIT:C156437 Repli-G X (Qiagen) DNA                                               A genomic DNA specimen amplified from an ultra-low-input sample using the REPLI-g X (Qiagen) whole genome amplification kit, designed for single-cell or trace-quantity starting material.                          NCIT:C156439 RNA                                                                  A biospecimen created to contain an isolated or enriched ribonucleic acid (RNA) sample.                                                                                                                             NCIT:C198568 Saliva                                                               The watery fluid in the mouth produced by the salivary glands that moistens food to aid digestion and helps protect the mouth against infection.                                                                    NCIT:C13275 Slides                                                               A biospecimen consisting of a tissue section or cell preparation mounted on a glass slide for microscopic examination.                                                                                              NCIT:C62755 Solid Tissue Normal                                                  A specimen of morphologically normal solid tissue collected from a subject, typically used as a matched normal control for a tumor specimen.                                                                        NCIT:C164014 Tissue                                                               An anatomical structure consisting of similarly specialized cells and intercellular matrix, aggregated according to genetically determined spatial relationships, that performs a specific function.                NCIT:C12801 Total RNA                                                            A biological sample comprised of all of the RNA collected from an experimental subject.                                                                                                                             NCIT:C163995 Tumor                                                                An abnormal mass of tissue that results from excessive cell division; used broadly to denote a neoplasm, which may be benign or malignant.                                                                          NCIT:C3262 Tumor Adjacent Normal - Post Neo-adjuvant Therapy                    A specimen of morphologically normal tissue collected from the area immediately surrounding a tumor, obtained from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic.                                        NCIT:C164033 Whole Animal                                                         Referring to the entire body of an experimental animal; used when a biospecimen consists of or is derived from an entire organism.                                                                                  NCIT:C77665 Whole Blood                                                          Blood that has not been separated into its various components, other than the addition of an anticoagulant.                                                                                                         NCIT:C41067 Xenograft Tissue                                                     Tissue derived from human or animal cells or tumor material that has been transplanted into and grown within a different (non-human) host organism.                                                                 NCIT:C122936 Unknown                                                              Not known, observed, recorded; or reported as unknown by the data contributor.                                                                                                                                      NCIT:C17998 Not Reported                                                         Not provided or available.                                                                                                                                                                                          NCIT:C43234

docs.title: Attribute: Biospecimen Composition
docs.text: Valid Value        Description                                                                                                  Ontology                                                                                              Metastatic         A tumor that has spread from its original site of growth to another anatomic site.                           NCIT:C3261 Not Applicable     Determination of a value is not relevant in the current context.                                             NCIT:C48660 Not Reported       An indication that the required information was not provided.                                                NCIT:C43234 Premalignant       A pathological process that precedes and often leads to the development of cancer.                           NCIT:C36032 Primary            A tumor at the original site at which it arose.                                                              NCIT:C8509 Prior Primary      Recurrent Disease, Primary Site                                                                              NCIT:C55072 Progression        Progressive Disease                                                                                          NCIT:C35571 Recurrent          The return of a disease after a period of remission.                                                         NCIT:C38155 Synchronous PrimaryMalignant Neoplasm of Multiple Primary Sites                                                                 NCIT:C35427 Unknown            Not known, observed, recorded, or reported as unknown by the data contributor.                               NCIT:C17998 Xenograft          A transplantation of cancer cells derived from an established cancer cell line into an immunodeficient mouse.NCIT:C156443

docs.title: Attribute: Biospecimen Preservation Method
docs.text: Valid Value                                         Description                                                                                                                                    Ontology                                                                                              Cryopreserved                                       Preservation of cells, tissues, organs, or embryos by storage at low temperatures.                                                             NCIT:C16475 Cytospin Slide                                      A slide prepared by centrifuging a cell suspension to concentrate cells onto the slide surface.                                                NCIT:C115350 Fixation                                            The chemical preservation of a substance to maintain structural and/or molecular features of that substance as they exist in the living entity.NCIT:C25219 Fresh                                               Tissue which has not been exposed to a fixative solution.                                                                                      NCIT:C84517 Fresh Dissociated                                   A tissue preparation process that takes fresh tissue and dissociates it into single cell suspensions.                                          NCIT:C185404 Fresh Dissociated and Single Cell Sorted            A tissue preparation process that separates fresh dissociated tissue cells into cell populations by single cell sorting.                       NCIT:C185405 Fresh Dissociated and Single Cell Sorted into PlatesA tissue preparation process that takes dissociated, sorted cells and distributes them into cell propagation plates.                           NCIT:C185406 Frozen                                              A tissue sample that has been frozen prior to analysis.                                                                                        NCIT:C158417 Not Applicable                                      Determination of a value is not relevant in the current context.                                                                               NCIT:C48660 Not Reported                                        An indication that the required information was not provided.                                                                                  NCIT:C43234 Refrigerated                                        A specimen that has been kept or preserved at a low temperature in a refrigerator.                                                             NCIT:C70718 Refrigerated Vacuum Chamber                         A device designed to maintain a vacuum at a below-ambient temperature.                                                                         NCIT:C185340 Snap Frozen                                         To freeze rapidly so as to preserve structure and prevent ice crystal formation.                                                               NCIT:C63521 Unknown                                             Not known, observed, recorded; or reported as unknown by the data contributor.                                                                 NCIT:C17998

docs.title: Attribute: Biospecimen Embedding Medium
docs.text: Valid Value           Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Ontology                                                                                            Paraffin wax          A common name for a group of high molecular weight alkane hydrocarbons; a white, odorless, tasteless, waxy solid widely used as an embedding medium for tissue processing in histology.                                                                  NCIT:C727 Carbowax              A trade name for polyethylene glycol (PEG), a water-soluble, wax-like polymer historically used as an embedding medium for light microscopy that allows sections to be stained without prior dewaxing.                                                   NCIT:C762 Methacrylate          A methyl ester of methacrylic acid; a reactive resin used as cement in dentistry, orthopaedic surgery, and ophthalmology, and as a hard plastic embedding medium for electron microscopy.                                                                NCIT:C47615 Epoxy Resin (Araldite)A class of thermosetting polymer resins (e.g., Araldite) formed by curing epoxide monomers with a hardener; used as a hard, transparent embedding medium for ultrathin sectioning in transmission electron microscopy.                                   MESH:D004853 Agar embedding        Use of agar, a gelatinous polysaccharide extracted from red algae, as a supporting medium to consolidate small, fragmented, or friable tissue specimens prior to histological processing and sectioning.                                                 MESH:D000362 Celloidin media       A purified nitrocellulose (collodion) solution in ether and alcohol; historically used as an embedding medium for sectioning large, hard, or heterogeneous specimens (e.g., whole organs, decalcified bone) that are poorly suited to paraffin embedding.MESH:D003101 Gelatin               A translucent, colorless, water-soluble protein derived from collagen; used as an embedding medium for cryosectioning and to orient or support small, friable tissue specimens.                                                                          NCIT:C65802 Other                 Different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.                                                                                                                                                                                             NCIT:C17649 None                  No person or thing, nobody, not any.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     NCIT:C41132 Unknown               Not known, observed, recorded, or reported as unknown by the data contributor.                                                                                                                                                                           NCIT:C17998

Its mission is to enable biomedical research, support health care and public health, and promote healthy behavior.                                                                                        NCIT:C82620 NCI Center for Cancer Research                                       Formed in Jan, 2001 by the merger of the Division of Clinical Sciences and the Division of Basic Sciences, the Center for Cancer Research is the largest component of the National Cancer Institute's Intramural Research Program.                                                                       NCIT:C20160 Purdue University Center for Cancer Research                         The mission of the Purdue University Center for Cancer Research is to promote discovery in the areas of biological phenomena, new chemical entities, and new technology that leads to the development of innovative instrumentation, new diagnostic tools, and novel therapeutics.                            NCIT:C39502 UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center                           The mission of the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center is to reduce cancer occurrence and death through research, treatment, training, and outreach. Designated as an NCI cancer center in 1975 and as a comprehensive cancer center in 1990.                                                          NCIT:C39554 Georgetown Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center                      The mission of the Georgetown Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center is to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer through innovative basic science, clinical research, patient care, community outreach, and the training of cancer specialists of the future.                              NCIT:C39530 National Clinical Trials Network                                     National Clinical Trials Network (NCI)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        NCIT:C217039 Proteogenomic Translational Research Centers                         Proteogenomic Translational Research Center                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   NCIT:C217040 Evelyn H. Lauder Founder’s Fund for Metastatic Breast Cancer ResearchAn international, multi-year collaboration to understand the molecular basis of metastasis in real people in real time. It aims to identify the molecular changes that occur as breast cancer evolves from a localized disease to one that has metastasized.                                                  NCIT:C217035 Center for Inherited Disease Research                                A program at Johns Hopkins University, supported by the National Cancer Institute, that supports the genetics community by providing high-quality, cutting edge genomics services and technologies in order to expand the understanding of disease and catalyze discoveries that translate to patient care.   NCIT:C217036 Transplant Recipients International Organization                     A not-for-profit, international organization committed to improving the quality of life for transplant candidates, transplant recipients, families of transplant candidates and recipients, and families of organ and tissue donors.                                                                          NCIT:C217041 Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation                                 A charitable organization that funds development and delivery of next-generation therapies, the leverage of data to identify optimal and more personalized treatment approaches, and empowers myeloma patients and the broader community with information and resources.                                      NCIT:C217038 Leukemia and Lymphoma Society                                        A charitable organization that is the largest non-profit funding source for blood cancer research around the world. It also provides free information and support services for patients and their families, and is an advocate for those seeking access to quality, affordable, coordinated care.             NCIT:C217037 Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology         A National Cancer Institute (NCI) Center that works to provide NCI staff and the cancer research community with the data science, information technology, and data sharing tools they need to advance the knowledge of cancer.                                                                                NCIT:C82329 Knight Cancer Institute                                              The mission of the Knight Cancer Institute is to translate discoveries into better ways to diagnose, prevent, and treat cancer. It became an NCI-designated Cancer Center in 1997.                                                                                                                            NCIT:C39343 Broad Institute                                                      A joint research venture of MIT and Harvard, established in 2004 to improve human health by using genomics to advance an understanding of the biology and treatment of human disease, and to help lay the groundwork for a new generation of therapies.
